facts.statement: Miogallus was an extinct genus of large pheasants that lived in Europe during the Miocene.
facts.quote: Miogallus is an extinct genus of large pheasant that lived during the Miocene of Europe.

facts.statement: The genus Miogallus contains only one species, Miogallus altus.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Miogallus altus.

facts.statement: Mlíkovský identified Miogallus altus, originally known as Miophasianus altus, after determining the genus Miophasianus was a nomen nudum.
facts.quote: Miogallus altus is better known as Miophasianus altus found by Mlíkovský who found the genus Miophasianus Lambrech in 1933 to be a nomen nudum.

facts.statement: Researchers consider Miogallus longaevus, described by Lambrecht in 1933, to be a likely junior synonym of Miogallus altus.
facts.quote: Even if the genus name Miophasianus was made available later by Brodkorb, we agree with Mlikovský that Miogallus longaevus Lambrecht, 1933 is very probably a junior synonym of M. altus.

facts.statement: The species is named Miogallus altus because the genus name Miogallus has priority over Miophasianus.
facts.quote: As a consequence of the priority of Miogallus Lambrecht, 1933 over Miophasianus Brodkorb, 1952, the species must be named Miogallus altus.

facts.statement: Miogallus belongs to the family Phasianidae.
The Paleobiology Database classifies Miogallus under the class Reptilia.
The type species for the genus Miogallus is listed as Gallus longaevus.
